deviations.what: the image latent sample uses explicit NumPy noise (drawn after the video and audio noise from the seed when not given)
deviations.why: diffusers samples latent_dist with its torch generator; the AGENTS.md determinism rule passes the same arrays to both sides, and the recorder patches DiagonalGaussianDistribution.sample for the run only (restored afterwards; tested)

deviations.what: tiled encoding (tiled_encode) is not ported; the image is always encoded in one pass
deviations.why: the pipeline encodes one frame and diffusers does not tile unless enable_tiling() is called. With the Baseline preset (which sets vae_tiling like the study notebook) diffusers would encode a 480x864 image in tiles, so Baseline I2V would differ from a diffusers run with tiling enabled; Smoke I2V is unaffected. Follow-up.

deviations.what: the relative frames rule of report 09 (bf16 frames PSNR within 1 dB of torch bf16) is not used for I2V
deviations.why: I2V meets the original absolute spec 09 criteria (per-step cosine >= 0.9996, frames 42-50 dB >= 30), which report 09 had to relax only for T2V. The relative rule would fail on 2 of 4 cases (MLX -1.4 and -4.5 dB vs torch bf16) while MLX is better on the other two (+0.3, +7.4 dB): at 40-50 dB both bf16 runs drift from float32 independently and the sign of their difference is not systematic. Stated here so the change of criterion is visible.

deviations.what: stage B uses our own generated frames as input images
deviations.why: no rights questions; they are natural-looking frames from the spec 10 Baseline video and a preset clip

follow_ups: Port tiled_encode for Baseline I2V with vae_tiling, or encode untiled and document the difference.
I2V presets of the study notebook (mario_*) need their reference images (owner's files).

architecture_notes.note: With a reference frame, bf16 drift over 10 PiFlow steps stays at per-step cosine >= 0.9996 and frames 42-50 dB vs float32, against cosine 0.993 and 27-46 dB for text-to-video (report 09): the clean tail frame anchors the trajectory.
architecture_notes.optimization: For I2V, bf16 is close to float32 quality; float32 matters less than for T2V.

architecture_notes.note: The tail frame adds one latent frame (7 -> 8 at Smoke, about +14% tokens): denoise 15.5 s vs 13.1 s for T2V. Encoding the image takes well under a second; the encoder is loaded from vae/model.safetensors per call and freed.
architecture_notes.optimization: Cache the encoder when generating several videos from images.

architecture_notes.note: The generated first frame reaches 31.8-38.7 dB PSNR against the preprocessed input image, identical between MLX and torch float32 to 0.01 dB; the model does not copy the input exactly (the tail frame conditions, it does not replace frame 0).
architecture_notes.optimization: None for the port; a pixel-exact first frame would need replacing frame 0 after decoding, which the reference does not do.
